finding.claim: Xxh32::update compares a u32-truncated input length against CHUNK_SIZE, then copies the full usize-length input into the 16-byte mem buffer. For slices of 4 GiB or more, this writes out of bounds (memory corruption in release builds, panic in debug builds).
finding.source: Caller-supplied input slice to the public safe Xxh32::update (src/xxh32.rs:102). Reachable only with a single slice of length >= 2^32 whose length mod 2^32 is small (or where mem_size + (len mod 2^32) wraps).
finding.sink: Buffer::copy_from_slice -> copy_from_slice_by_size -> ptr::copy_nonoverlapping into self.mem ([u32;4], 16 bytes) at src/utils.rs:48.

trace.note: update(input: &[u8]) entry; input.len() is usize and may exceed u32::MAX
total_len accumulates input.len() as u32 (truncating; intended for digest)
(mem_size + input.len() as u32) < 16 — truncated width; e.g. len=2^32+5, mem_size=0 gives 5 < 16 and takes the small-copy branch
copy_from_slice passes src.len() (full length) to copy_from_slice_by_size
only check is debug_assert on self.len - offset >= len; compiled out in release
copy_nonoverlapping writes len bytes (~4 GiB) into a 16-byte buffer

finding.guards_checked: CHUNK_SIZE comparison exists but operates in truncated u32 width, so it does not bound the copy length. No input.len() <= u32::MAX check on the path. Buffer::copy_from_slice relies only on debug_assert. Not affected: xxh64.rs:116-168 (u64 mem_size, usize arithmetic); xxh3 streaming xxh3.rs:888-939 (usize check before u16 cast, buffer <=256). Not reproduced by execution; verified by reading.
